data.name: label1.Text
data.value: Braille works by using a system of raised dots that can be felt with the fingertips. Each Braille character is formed within a small rectangular grid made up of two columns and three rows, creating positions where dots can either be raised or left empty. By plotting different combinations of raised dots within this grid, letters, numbers, punctuation marks, and other symbols can be represented. The dots can be produced by pressing or punching holes into paper so that the opposite side forms raised bumps, allowing the reader to identify each character through touch. By arranging these Braille cells next to one another, complete words, sentences, and other forms of written information can be created.
